rendered: The BatPaC scenario is an electric vehicle with a range of 260 miles[1] and a battery pack energy of ≈76.47 kWh[2], scaled to the projected fleet of 1 000 000 EVs[3] on the road by 2030[4]. In that scenario the cobalt needed with the mainstream cathode NMC 111[5] is ≈2500 tons[6], while the next-generation cathodes NMC 811[7] and NCA would still require ≈700 tons[8] of cobalt. Dividing the first figure by the second, the mainstream cathode needs about 3.6[9] times as much cobalt as the next-generation cathodes in that scenario.
